fields.meta_title: Video Landing Page Examples and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a video landing page that starts muted with captions, shows the button at the right second, and saves how long each lead watched.
fields.h1: Build a Video Landing Page That Turns Viewers Into Leads
fields.hero_description: Build a video landing page that plays muted with captions and saves how much of the video each lead watched.
fields.features_heading: What Sits Around the Video Player
fields.features_subheading: The video makes the pitch. The page around it decides whether a viewer becomes a lead, and keeps a record of what each one saw.
fields.feature_1:
A poster frame that loads before the video

Until the video starts, the player shows a still you pick, such as the speaker mid-sentence. The headline loads first, and the video file waits until the player nears the screen.
fields.feature_2:
A muted start with captions on

Captions run from a WebVTT file attached to the video. The video starts muted when it scrolls into view, and a single tap on the sound icon brings the speaker's voice in.
fields.feature_3:
A button timed to a second of the video

Set the timestamp where the order button appears. Before that second, the page shows only the video and headline. Afterward it stays on screen, even if the visitor pauses.
fields.feature_4:
Watch time saved with every lead

Emergent writes each lead to a database you own, along with the seconds watched and the furthest point reached. Sort by watch time, or sync new rows to any CRM with an API.
fields.feature_5:
Your own file or a YouTube link

Upload the video file, or paste a YouTube link and keep its player. Both report each play and pause to the page, which saves them against the visit that produced them.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take elsewhere

The page and its lead table export to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Run the code on your own servers, or publish on Emergent at a custom domain, which uses credits.

fields.usecase_heading: Video Landing Page Examples by Format
fields.tab_content_1:
The Enroll button stays hidden until the price is named

Lumen Coaching sells a $297 course on pricing freelance work through a 22-minute video sales letter. The Enroll button stays off the page until 14:20, the moment the price comes up. Last month 1,840 visitors pressed play. Of those, 612 reached the offer and 87 enrolled.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every trial tagged with the seconds of demo watched

Above the trial form on Tallyhand's home page, a 90-second demo of its invoicing app plays muted, with captions on. Each trial sign-up is saved with how many seconds of the demo that visitor watched. Of last month's 214 trials, 131 came from people who got past 60 seconds.
fields.tab_content_3:
One customer story behind 58 of 97 quote requests

Homeowners pick from three customer videos on Harbor Roofing's quote page. The request form saves which video each homeowner played first. Last month the hail damage repair story sat behind 58 of the 97 requests, and the crew now books those inspections before anything else.
fields.tab_content_4:
Halfway in, Dana's rep gets a direct message

Two minutes of video sit at the top of a page that Quillfield Analytics rep Owen Castillo made for one prospect, Dana Reyes at Maplestone Freight. The page greets her by name. Once she passes the one-minute mark, Owen gets a direct message in Slack showing how far she watched.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Video Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a video landing page that loads fast on any screen and shows which viewers went on to sign up.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the one job the video does
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Keep the offer readable without sound
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the video is for before you script a line. A sales letter carries the whole pitch and runs as long as the pitch needs. A product demo shows one task being done, and a customer story makes one claim believable.
fields.howto_step_2_des: A visitor who never presses play still needs the offer. Put the headline and the main call to action beside or under the video, and write the headline so it makes sense on its own. The video adds proof; the page carries the ask.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Without a poster attribute, the player stays blank until the first frame arrives. Pick a still with a face or the product on screen. When the video sits at the top, its poster can be the page's Largest Contentful Paint element. Compress it like any hero image.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Chrome lets a video start on its own when it is muted, and usually holds back sound until the visitor interacts with the site. Pair autoplay with muted and playsinline, which keeps the video in place on an iPhone. Put a clear sound control on the video itself.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Captions carry the pitch for everyone watching with the sound off. Attach a WebVTT file through the track element, then check it against the audio. WCAG lists captions for prerecorded video as a Level A criterion, its most basic level of conformance.
fields.howto_step_6_des: An embedded player is heavy, and a page with three of them loads all three on arrival. Add loading="lazy" to iframes below the first screen, which defers each one until the visitor scrolls near it. For a file you host, preload="none" holds the download until play.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Record plays, then test the video
fields.howto_step_7_des: Save play, pause, and end events with each lead: the YouTube player API reports state changes, and an HTML video fires its own events. Then run the page with and without the video for the same traffic, and keep the version that brings in more sign-ups.

plan.angle: The top 10 is example roundups (SaaS Landing Page, Wyzowl, Swarmify, ConvertFlow), a Dribbble gallery, Pexels stock clips, an Unbounce benefits article, a YouTube tutorial and a Reddit thread asking whether video helps at all. They show what a video landing page looks like and stop at the play button. This page defines the term for the AI Overview, then shows four working video landing pages sorted by the job the video does (sales letter, product demo, customer stories, a one-to-one sales video), each with what the page records about the watching, plus a how-to grounded in browser autoplay policy, the HTML video element, captions, lazy loading and the YouTube player API.

scope.evidence: H1 "Build a Video Landing Page That Turns Viewers Into Leads"; hero "Build a video landing page that plays muted with captions and saves how much of the video each lead watched." (108 chars); how-to description one sentence, 112 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is example roundups and an AI Overview. Item 1 defines the term, the tabs give four working examples by format (VSL, demo, customer stories, personal video), and the how-to covers autoplay, captions, poster, lazy loading and play events.

specificity.evidence: Video vocabulary: "WebVTT file", "poster attribute", "playsinline", "preload=\"none\"", "14:20, the moment the price comes up".

openers.evidence: Body paragraphs open on full sentences ("Until a visitor presses play...", "Homeowners pick from three customer videos..."); one FAQ fragment opener recorded as a note.

craft.evidence: QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean; one idea per sentence ("Of those, 612 reached the offer and 87 enrolled.").

voice.evidence: Concrete detail: "a $297 course on pricing freelance work", "131 came from people who got past 60 seconds", "the crew now books those inspections before anything else". Shared sibling formulas recorded as a note.

truth.evidence: feature_1 "The headline and the button load first, and the video file waits for the click." contradicts feature_2 "The video starts muted when it scrolls into view" (and hero, meta, tab 2) and feature_3 "Before that second, the page shows only the video and headline".

distinct.evidence: No sibling primary (mobile, QR code, animated, modern landing page) in any heading or answer; the tabs are sorted by the video's job.

faq.evidence: Exactly 10 on-topic questions, no brands or formats in questions; hub link in item 2; two sibling links (webinar-landing-page, thank-you-page); all 10 secondaries placed; F9 lines in items 7, 8 and 10; autoplay facts sourced to Chrome and WebKit.

findings.quote: The headline and the button load first, and the video file waits for the click.
findings.issue: Two fields describe the same built page in opposite ways. (1) feature_1: "Until a visitor presses play, the player shows a still you pick" and "the video file waits for the click". Against it: feature_2 "The video starts muted when it scrolls into view", hero_description "plays muted with captions", meta_description "starts muted with captions", and tab_content_2 "a 90-second demo ... plays muted". A muted autoplay never waits for a click. (2) feature_1 "the button load[s] first" against feature_3 "Before that second, the page shows only the video and headline" and tab_content_1 "The Enroll button stays off the page until 14:20".
findings.fix: Rewrite feature_1 (165-182 chars) so it holds with muted autoplay and the timed button. For example: "Until the video starts, the player shows a still you pick, such as the speaker mid-sentence. The headline loads first, and the video file waits until the player scrolls into view." Then search the page again for any other click-to-load wording.
